TAL_SCOUNDREL_STEAL.why: The printed lines run at the table. The check is combat/ext/tabik_scoundrel.py's scoundrel_check: an aware target is opposed in Athletics or Acrobatics (the better one, ties to the defender), an unaware one is beaten by Passive Perception, and the chosen object carries the printed Disadvantage when it is worn or held in two hands unless Master Thief waives it. "Choose one accessible object" comes FIRST, because the printed difficulty and the printed result are both about that object: combat/ext/scoundrel_riders.py steal_object_choice answers the scoundrel_object_choice seam before the check rolls, offering what the target actually has on it now (a complete suit of worn armor is not ordinarily accessible, as Master Thief prints) and the thief's own Tiny things to plant -- the printed size is asked, because this table keeps no object sizes -- and the rows it returns run only when the check succeeds, so a failed check hands over nothing. "Take nothing", and declining, are answers too: the check is still made, because it is what the action is, but no object moves and the row's own default disarm does not happen instead. Each pick is applied as this table's own record of gear, ONE record per object, filed on the creature whose bundle lists it and moved in place by _transfer_record on every later handover, so the object keeps its own name and weight, never has two homes at once, and a saved fight replays it: held_by naming the hand it went into, or combat/carry.py's own dropped-item record for "cause the object to fall into an unoccupied space within your reach", so both loads are reweighed. Only when nobody answers at all -- an engine with no choice transport, or a fight saved before the seam -- does the row keep its own default, the local Scoundrel disarm of the best weapon in hand (steal_weapon). "Steal does not automatically activate, identify, attune to, or safely handle the object" needs no rule: the table hands the object over and nothing else. A2SCOUNDRE: newly compiled object_locations=1 opts into a reposition result and hand/carried-location choice. One existing identity record follows each relocated object; same-owner relocation retains load and a stowed weapon loses its attack. Markerless saved rows keep their previous choices.

effects.evidence: Once per turn, after you spend Qi on a feature that resolves successfully, choose one. Perfected: Choose two different benefits.
The target immediately repeats the saving throw with Advantage. On success, apply the effect's normal successful-save result.

riders: Meridian Regulation is resolved by the table, one question for both of its printed branches. Choose one of the target's poisons, diseases or physical impairments. If that effect makes the target repeat a saving throw, the target repeats that throw with Advantage, and a successful repeat applies the effect's own successful result. If the effect does not repeat its save, the target makes a Constitution saving throw with Advantage against that effect's printed DC (the number the throw has to beat), and on a success one of that effect's penalties -- Poisoned, a Speed reduction, Disadvantage on attack rolls, Disadvantage on ability checks, Disadvantage on saving throws, or an inability to take Reactions -- stops applying until the end of the target's next turn. Effects of either kind are all offered in the same question, so an effect that repeats its save never hides another effect from the printed choice. The fighter chooses which one.

The effect must be a poison, a disease, or a directly caused physical impairment before either branch is offered, and that is decided from the effect's own ability and its printed text, never from the penalty it happens to leave: a dream, an illusion or a sound that leaves one of the penalties below is still not one of those three. The fight keeps a reviewed list of the printed abilities that can leave such an effect, one entry for each ability with the sentence from the rules that decides it: an entry either places that ability in one of the three, or records that the ability stays the GM's to rule on. An ability that is on neither list is the GM's to rule on as well.

The two printed limits are checked before anything is offered: the effect must have a printed saving throw DC, and it must not carry the Curse, Tribulation, Foundation Injury, Hidden Injury, Possession, Permanent or Soul Damage tag. An effect with no printed DC, or one whose printed text the fight cannot identify, is the GM's to rule on. Source-owned Disadvantage on attack rolls is selectable alongside the other printed penalties; suppressing one penalty preserves the effect's other penalties and ongoing damage.

Meridian Regulation does not automatically remove the underlying effect, end its duration, cure the disease or poison, remove Exhaustion, restore Hit Points, stop ongoing damage, or remove a higher-authority effect.
